Execution and financing risk offsets the upside. The 2026 guide needs ARR to rise 2.3-3x in H2, and only about 1 GW of 5 GW contracted power will be connected by year-end. Capex of $20-25B and a GAAP loss imply heavy funding needs, while the roughly $52B market cap is about 6.5x the guided ARR midpoint.

parsed.rationale: At $235.88 the market cap is about $52B, roughly 6.5x the midpoint of 2026 ARR guidance, before debt that will fund $20-25B of capex. Pricing, sold-out capacity and strong payback economics justify a premium. However, the H2 ARR ramp is steep, power connection lags contracted capacity, and the GAAP loss and funding needs add risk. Growth looks largely priced in, so the stock looks roughly fairly valued.

Competition and financing quality cap the multiple. Broadcom's custom-accelerator revenue is growing very fast and is guided to about $115B for FY27. Nvidia also backstops customers such as CoreWeave, which looks circular and adds credit risk.

Supply and cost constraints affect timing and margins but are easing or are priced in. Grid and power delays could push out data-centre build-outs. The CoWoS packaging gap is narrowing. A 121% rise in HBM prices in 2027 could pressure margins.

parsed.rationale: At $228.38 and a ~$5.5T market cap, NVDA trades at roughly 16-20x annualised earnings implied by the >$104B data-centre quarter and 76%+ gross margin. Capex and rental-price evidence suggests demand stays strong near term. I apply about 22x to estimated earnings of roughly $280B for a fair value near $262. Upside is limited by custom-ASIC competition (Broadcom), circular customer financing, HBM cost inflation and power-delay risk. The stock is moderately undervalued, but earnings are cyclical and peak-like, so confidence is moderate.

drivers.claim: Quarterly results and guidance imply a low run-rate multiple. Data-centre revenue was $89.0B (+117%), gross margin 75%, and next-quarter revenue is guided to $108B, an annualised run-rate above $400B. Against a roughly $5.5T market cap ($228.38 per share), that is about low-20s times run-rate earnings, with Vera Rubin ramping.

Demand and supply data point to continued tightness. Hyperscaler capex is about $646B in 2026, H100 one-year rental prices rose almost 40% with capacity sold out and booked through Aug-Sep 2026, and CoWoS and HBM constraints persist. This supports pricing and volume near term.

Offsetting risks cap the upside. Custom ASICs are growing fast (Broadcom AI revenue +221%, guided to about $115B for FY27), Nvidia's circular financing and backstops add credit exposure, and power and grid delays could push data-centre capacity into 2027 or later.

parsed.rationale: At $228.38, NVDA trades at roughly 22x annualised current earnings, with 75% gross margins, 117% data-centre growth and guidance still rising. Capex, rental pricing and packaging data show demand ahead of supply. I assume FY28 EPS of about $11-12 at roughly 23-25x, giving a fair value near $265, so the stock looks moderately undervalued. Risks are custom-silicon share gains, vendor-financing exposure (CoreWeave backstop), power-grid delays, rising HBM costs, and the cyclicality shown by the 2024 rental price collapse. Confidence is moderate.

Customer prepayments covering 50 to 60% of capex on about 70% of deals and paybacks under two years partly mitigate funding risk.

drivers.claim: Leverage and losses weigh on the equity. Q2 2026 net loss was $626M, net interest expense of $640M exceeded operating profit, total debt is $35.1B with a refinancing wall in 2026-2028, and the market cap of about $40B sits beneath roughly $75B of enterprise value on guidance of $12.4-13.2B revenue (about 5.9x EV/sales).

Demand and pricing support is strong. The $104.2B backlog and H100 one-year rental prices up about 40% to $2.35/GPU-hour, with capacity booked through September 2026, point to durable near-term revenue visibility.

Concentration, circular financing and cyclicality limit the upside. Top three customers are about 72% of revenue, Nvidia both invests in CoreWeave equity and backstops $6.3B of unsold capacity, GPU rental prices fell sharply in 2024 after a capacity wave, and Nebius has joined the Platinum tier that competes on cost of ownership.

parsed.rationale: At $87.12 the shares trade near $40B market cap, and the packet shows a loss-making, heavily indebted business with rising interest costs exceeding operating profit. Offsetting this, the $104B backlog and tight GPU rental pricing give good visibility. At about $52B market capitalisation, the shares trade near 16x the $3.2B midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance, while 2026 capex of $20-25B far exceeds adjusted EBITDA of $236M per quarter and the GAAP net loss was $190M; prepayments covering 50-60% of capex mitigate but do not remove funding risk, so the valuation looks full rather than cheap.

parsed.rationale: At $235.88 (market cap about $52B), NBIS looks roughly fairly valued on this packet. Pricing momentum is strong and new contracts reportedly pay back in under two years, but the ARR guidance needs a 2.3-3x rise in H2 with only about 1 GW of 5 GW connected, and 2026 capex of $20-25B far exceeds current adjusted EBITDA. Market cap is roughly 16x the 2026 revenue guidance midpoint. The packet includes secondary coverage and a news item labelled synthetic, and it lacks net debt and cash data, limiting confidence. The fair value estimate of about $245 assumes modest upside from pricing while discounting execution risk.

Broadcom's AI revenue grew 221% year on year, is 73% custom XPUs, and is guided to about $115B for fiscal 2027 with Google, OpenAI and Meta as customers. TrendForce projects HBM prices to rise 121% in 2027, which could squeeze gross margins.

Deployment and credit risks could cap upside at a market cap of about $5.5T. 30-50% of the remaining 11GW of 2026 US data-centre capacity may slip to 2027 or later because of grid delays. CoWoS constraints are easing, which could loosen scarcity. Nvidia also carries vendor-financing exposure, including a $6.3B CoreWeave backstop.

parsed.rationale: At $228.38, about a $5.5T market cap, NVDA prices in sustained AI dominance. The packet contains no NVDA earnings, margin or guidance figures, so the fair value cannot be derived from fundamentals and is a judgment call. Demand signals are strong: record hyperscaler capex and tight GPU rental markets. These are offset by Broadcom's fast-growing custom-accelerator business, rising HBM input costs, grid-driven deployment slippage, easing packaging scarcity and circular financing exposure. Weighing these, I judge the shares roughly fairly valued with slight downside risk. My fair value is about $220, held with low confidence given the missing financials.

Demand backdrop is supportive: one-year H100 rental prices rose about 40% to $2.35 per GPU-hour, capacity is sold out, and anchor contracts with Microsoft (about $9.7B) and NVIDIA (about $3.4B) underpin the contracted revenue.

parsed.rationale: Market cap of about $16B at $40.88 compares with only about $1B of the roughly $4B contracted annualised revenue operating today and $128.8M of FY2026 AI Cloud revenue. A nine-month deferral moving about $600M of FY2027 revenue into FY2028, plus the company's own warning that contracted revenue is not fully contracted, lowers near-term visibility. Demand indicators are strong: GPU rental prices rose about 40% and capacity is sold out, and anchor contracts with Microsoft and NVIDIA total about $13.1B. Still, valuation rests on unbuilt capacity and unpriced execution risk, so the stock looks modestly unattractive. The packet has no margin, cash flow or debt data, so the fair value estimate is low confidence.

drivers.claim: Strong GPU demand and pricing support Nebius's growth and unit economics. H100 one-year rental prices rose almost 40%, Nebius raised on-demand prices in September, and its Platinum ClusterMAX rating supports premium pricing.

At about a $52B market cap, the stock trades near 6-7x year-end ARR guidance of $7-9B and roughly 16x 2026 revenue guidance. That looks reasonable only if hypergrowth and the claimed economics (>$20M revenue per MW, <2-year payback, 41% adjusted EBITDA margin) hold.
